family_reports.body: The hardest lesson I learned in family court was that patterns do not disappear just because they are ignored. When abuse is treated as an isolated incident, evidence becomes negotiable, opinions become powerful, and accountability becomes optional. That is when I realized the abuse had not disappeared. It had simply found another face.

This system removed my children without due process, ignored evidence that cleared me, and created financial and procedural barriers that have kept me separated from them for years. The court actors built a system where I have to pay thousands just to try to be their mom again.

public_comments.comment_text: During her time representing me, she was also serving as a Guardian ad Litem (GAL) for other parents, and it became clear that she was overly familiar with others within the system. Furthermore, she failed to advocate for me, frequently accepting my ex-partner's claims without consulting or believing me. I fired her and I retained my former attorney, who has previously provided excellent representation.
